title_he: מֵאָז כִּבְּדַנִי אֲדֹנִי בְּמַבָּט בָּשִׂים אֵלַי
review: 1:3–4 and 2:3–4 are identical in the print (قَلْبِي امْتَلَا حُبًّا سَمَا / كَأَنِّي دَوْمًا فِي السَّمَا), and the payload repeats the two lines verbatim, so the refrain closes both stanzas. This is the hymn's device: the second stanza changes only its cause, not its conclusion.

3:3–3:4 שָׁוֶה הוּא לִי, כִּי אֲנִי אוֹרֵחַ — the Arabic سِيَّانِ عِنْدِي إِنَّنِي / ضَيْفٌ مُعَدٌّ لِلسَّمَا is 'alike to me, for I am a guest bound for heaven'; the Hebrew keeps the 'guest' (אוֹרֵחַ, as in 2 Sam 12:4) and the 'prepared/bound' participle, so the indifference to palace or hut rests on destination, not on Stoic detachment.

4:2–4:4 מָעוֹז טוֹב … הַמּוֹלִיךְ נַפְשִׁי שָׁמָיְמָה — the Arabic خَيْرُ حِمَى … يَهْدِي نَفْسِي لِلسَّمَا is 'best shelter … guiding my soul heavenward'; the Hebrew keeps מָעוֹז as the psalm's refuge (Ps 27:1) and the Hiphil 'lead up' (Ps 107:7, וַיַּדְרִיכֵם בְּדֶרֶךְ יְשָׁרָה).

5:1–5:3 כְּבוֹדִי שִׂמְחָתִי וְעֶדְנִי … אֲשֶׁר פָּדַנִי וַיָּשֶׂם — the Arabic مَجْدِي سُرُورِي لَذَّتِي … مَنْ قَدْ فَدَانِي جَاعِلًا is a threefold self-description followed by the ransoming agent; the Hebrew keeps both halves and the singular verb, so the praise still belongs to the One who acted.

1:1–1:2 כָּבוֹד לְמוֹחֵה הָעָוֹן / טִהֲרַנִי עַד־תָּמִים — the Arabic مَجْدًا لِمَنْ مَحَا الْآثَام / طَهَّرَنِي إِلَى التَّمَام is 'glory to Him who wiped out sins, who cleansed me to completeness'; the Hebrew keeps מָחָה ('blot out', Ps 51:3, Isa 43:25) and עַד־תָּמִים, so both the blotting and the thoroughness are stated.
